data.description:
# Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item pane existence

## Problem statement

The "in progress" marker shown in the Herdr selection list is unreliable: it is
derived from the worklog `in-progress` status, which is maintained by the
hydrator — a self-healing loop that decides whether a claimed item is genuinely
being worked on. Every interactive/downtime dispatch now spawns an agent pane
whose **title carries the exact work-item ID** as a preserved trailing suffix
(`pane-title.ts`, `truncatePaneTitlePreservingSuffix`). The hydrator's active
detection must be a single simple rule: if there is a pane in this workspace
with the work item id (as part of) its title the item is being worked on; if
there is no such pane it is not.

> Producer review (2026-10-16): "This isn't reliable at present. review the
> algorith. It should be simple. Look for a pane in this workspace with the work
> item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy. If it doesn't then
> it is not busy."
>
> An earlier revision matched the exact **label** of a workspace **tab**
> (`herdr tab list`). That proved unreliable: tabs are created by the dispatcher
> *anchor* as a placement side effect, so an item being dispatched can be
> evaluated before its tab exists (a false-demotion race), and tabs can be
> re-parented or renamed. Pane **titles** are set at spawn time, always carry
> the item ID as a preserved suffix, and survive re-parenting — matching them
> is the reliable signal this work item implements.

## Users

- Herdr operator selecting the next work item from the selection list.
- Downtime dispatcher / plugin panes that rely on the hydrator to release stale
  `in-progress` claims so the item re-enters the dispatchable pool.

Example user stories:

- As a Herdr operator, I want the selection list's in-progress marker to reflect
  reality — an item is "being worked on" iff a pane in my workspace has the
  work-item ID in its title — so I can trust the list without opening panes.
- As a dispatched agent, I want my claimed item left `in-progress` for as long
  as my work-item pane is open, so my claim is never released underneath me.
- As an operator, I want a stale claim (no work-item pane) released
  automatically and periodically so abandoned items return to the dispatchable
  pool.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An item is treated as actively worked **iff** a pane in the current
      workspace (`HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, or `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`)
      has a title **containing** the work-item ID (the dispatched pane titles
      always carry the ID as a preserved suffix). A pane title with no work-item
      ID contributes nothing. Verified by unit tests over a pure
      pane-title-matching helper.
- [ ] The hydrator's active detection is `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` +
      pane-title ID extraction; the pane-matching seam/types (`HydratorPane`,
      `listActivePanes`, `collectPaneWorkItemIds`, `isActivePaneMatch`) are used.
      Verified by code review + updated `hydrator.test.ts` (a `herdr pane list`
      spawn asserted; no `herdr tab list` spawn for active detection).
- [ ] Demotion rules are unchanged: a non-active item at stage `in_review` →
      `completed`/`in_review`; a non-active item with an active outbound blocker
      → `blocked`; otherwise → `open` (stage repaired to a compatible value). An
      item with a matching pane is never demoted. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] The signal is refreshed periodically from the selection list: the existing
      30 s hydrate task (`HYDRATOR_INTERVAL_MS`) and the hidden→visible
      focus-resume hook both re-evaluate pane existence, so a closed work-item
      pane clears the marker within one cadence and an opened pane keeps it.
      Verified by existing scheduler/visibility tests plus a pane-based
      hydration test.
- [ ] Fail-open preserved: an unavailable/unparseable `herdr pane list` aborts
      the cycle without demoting, and panes outside the current workspace never
      mark an item active. Verified by unit tests.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (notably the
      hydrator module header and the `pane-title.ts` rationale comment).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Do not change the worklog status/stage vocabulary or the demotion outcome
  rules.
- Keep the bounded/responsive hydrator contract (per-step timeout, per-tick
  cap, stdio isolation, fail-open) unchanged; only the "which items are active"
  lookup changes.
- Reuse the existing pane parsing/seam where possible rather than adding a
  second parser for the same CLI shape.
- Retain exports still used elsewhere: `extractWorkItemIdsFromText`
  (`ship-guard.ts`) and `isActiveBlocker` (`stalled-work.ts`).
- No CLI or socket API change; `herdr pane list` is already used by the plugin.
- Write in UK English; follow the project's test/build conventions.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — fetches `wl list --status in-progress`,
  fetches live panes (`herdr pane list [--workspace <id>]`), collects work-item
  IDs from pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`), and demotes items with no
  matching pane. Exposes pure helpers (`collectPaneWorkItemIds`,
  `isActivePaneMatch`, `decideDemotion`, `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — creates the hydrator runner with
  `workspaceId: process.env.HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, runs it every 30 s (`hydrate`
  task) and on hidden→visible focus-resume. The selection list's in-progress
  marker (`statusIcon(item.status)`) and Group N ordering (`status ===
  'in-progress'`) are driven by the worklog status this loop maintains plus the
  pane-based display marker (`applyActivePaneMarkers`).
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — truncation helpers that preserve the
  work-item ID as a trailing suffix so the pane-title match is always reliable.

## Desired change

The hydrator's "is this item active" signal is pane-title existence:

1. A pure helper returns the set of work-item IDs present in the current
   workspace's pane titles (`collectPaneWorkItemIds(tabs)` /
   `isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes)`).
2. `HydratorDeps.listActivePanes(workspaceId)` is backed by
   `herdr pane list --workspace <id>`.
3. `runHydrationOnce` uses pane membership; `decideDemotion`,
   `compatibleStage`, `isActiveBlocker`, `extractWorkItemIdsFromText` and the
   bounded-run machinery are unchanged.
4. Tests and the module/doc comments describe pane-title detection.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — pane-title matching seam/types/helpers.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — hydrator wiring (workspace id, cadence,
  focus-resume, `active-pane-marker` task).
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.test.ts` — pane-title cases; exact, workspace-
  scope and fail-open cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.fixtures.ts` — pane fixtures + `pane list` exec
  router answer.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator-responsiveness.test.ts` — updated to the
  pane-based deps.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-title.ts` — rationale comment for tile-title
  detection.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `applyActivePaneMarkers` production wiring.

## Related work

- WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI — Herdr hydrator: rescue `in_progress` work items with no
  active pane (parent of the hydrator design).
- WL-0MTF5WO2Q008B8US — Hydrator: demote stale `in_progress` items.
- WL-0MUY1CXSV008F8TZ / WL-0MUY1CYCB003DTKO / WL-0MUY1CYV6008BQWX — bounded/
  isolated hydrate steps (contract to preserve).
- WL-0MUKXFWLD006A8XI / WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — item-ID tab anchor and dispatch
  wiring (tab-per-item convention; panes inherit the ID-titled anchor).
- WL-0MUY1CS9E006ZLS0 — re-based Herdr in-progress UI behaviour on `status`.
- WL-0MSBQUJQX005RAT9 — per-row agent-status icon (separate feature).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (scope):** "the logic for discovering when an item is being
  worked on" is the hydrator's active detection; the selection-list in-progress
  marker follows from the status the hydrator maintains plus the injected
  pane-title display marker.
- **Assumption:** pane titles carry the exact work-item ID as a trailing suffix
  for every dispatch path (manual, shell, downtime builders), so a
  contains-match is correct and robust; no substring false positives because the
  ID token is matched exactly.
- **Assumption:** `herdr pane list --workspace <id>` returns
  `result.panes[].label` (the pane title), as parsed by the shared
  `parseMachinePaneListOutput`; no new herdr capability is required.
- **Risk:** a pane may outlive its agent (kept open after the agent finishes),
  leaving an item `in-progress`. This matches the requested rule (pane = worked
  on); operators close the pane to release the item.
- **Scope-creep risk:** sharing the signal with `AgentTracker` or the
  agent-status icon is a linked follow-up item, not part of this change.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-10-10 — Created three children (core/verification/docs) and wired
  dependency edges.
- 2026-10-14 — Producer directed tab-label exact matching
  (commit 73463773).
- 2026-10-16 — Producer rejected the tab-label formulation as unreliable and
  directed pane-title matching: "Look for a pane in this workspace with the
  work item id as the title. If it exists then work item is busy." Rework
  updated the hydrator (tab-label → pane-title), the marker, tests, fixtures
  and docs accordingly.
data.title: Herdr selection list: base the in-progress marker on work-item tab existence

# Blocking item status (WL-0MVBMLY2Z0032CYR)

**Headline:** The Herdr `Blocked By` metadata rows (selection-list preview) currently show only the blocker's ID and title, discarding the `status` field that `wl dep list` already returns; the detail view shows no `Blocked By` rows at all. Show each blocker's status (icon + text) in the preview rows AND add equivalent `Blocked By` rows (with status) to the detail view, reversing the documented WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP AC-5 divergence.

## Problem statement

When a user selects a dependency-blocked item, the Herdr metadata panel tells them *what* is blocking it (`Blocked By  WL-xxx — <title>`) but not the blocker's current `status` (e.g. `in_progress`, `open`, `blocked`), and the detail view shows no blocker information at all. A producer who sees a blocked item cannot tell at a glance whether the blocker is already being worked, still open, or itself stuck — the "blocked" signal is incomplete. The status data is already returned by `wl dep list <id> --json` but `fetchBlockersForItem` discards it.

## Users

- **Producers / triage engineers** browsing the Herdr selection list who need to know whether a blocker is actively being worked before deciding to escalate or re-prioritise.
- **Dispatch operators** inspecting a blocked candidate who need the blocker's state without leaving the pane.
- **Reviewers** opening the detail view who expect the same blocker visibility the preview offers.

### Example user stories

- As a **producer**, I want to see the status of each item blocking the selected item in the metadata panel, so that I can tell at a glance whether the blocker is in progress, open, or itself blocked.
- As a **dispatch operator**, I want the blocker's status shown with the same icon+text convention as every other meta row, so I can scan the panel quickly without parsing text.
- As a **reviewer**, I want the detail view to show `Blocked By` rows (with blocker status) just like the preview, so I don't split context between the two surfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The selection-list metadata panel renders each active blocker row as `Blocked By  WL-xxxxxxxx — <title> <blocker-status-icon> <blocker-status>` (icon + text suffix), consistent with the Status/Stage/Priority row convention (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9); an existing blocker row without a status in the parsed edge still renders the ID + title (status appended only when present).
- [ ] The Herdr detail view renders the same active `Blocked By` rows — one row per blocker with ID, title and status (icon + text) — placed after the metadata section, reversing the documented divergence (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP AC-5).
- [ ] No-versus-some is preserved: when the selected item has no active blockers, both the preview and the detail view are unchanged (no `Blocked By` rows anywhere).
- [ ] Icon gating is honoured: when icons are disabled (`noIcons`, as in the existing meta rows), the blocker status renders as plain text only (no emoji), consistent with every other meta row.
- [ ] `BlockerRef` carries the blocker's `status`; `fetchBlockersForItem` passes the edge's `status` through (it is already on the `wl dep list` edge — no additional lookup or process spawns).
- [ ] Detail-view blocker lookup is fail-open and non-breaking: a failed/unparseable `wl dep list` lookup yields no `Blocked By` rows in the detail view and never breaks rendering, scrolling or navigation; the detail view's async lookup is single-flight with the existing pattern and does not re-open the WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP flicker class.
- [ ] The detail view's scroll bounds (`detailScrollOffset` clamp, `formatDetailContent`/`formatDetail` height calc) account for the new `Blocked By` rows so they are reachable when the view scrolls.
- [ ] Unit tests cover: preview renders blocker status (icon + text); blocker without status still renders ID + title; detail view renders active blockers with status; detail view omits rows when none; terminal blockers stay filtered by `isActiveBlocker`; fail-open path for both surfaces.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `packages/herdr/README.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Status source is the `wl dep list` edge only** — no new `wl` process spawns (no per-blocker `wl show` for status; the existing stage-enrichment lookups for the active-blocker predicate stay as they are).
- **Reuse existing helpers:** `isActiveBlocker()` (`packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts`), `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`), `statusIcon()` (`packages/shared/src/icons.ts`), and the metadata row/icon conventions (`buildMetaRows`, WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9).
- **Fail-open everywhere:** dependency look-up errors degrade to "no `Blocked By` rows", never a thrown error in the render path (consistent with the preview's existing behaviour).
- **No list-data shape regression:** `WorkItem` consumers (list rows, filters, dispatch) must be unaffected by any added optional field.
- **No new dependency edges are created or mutated** — read-only display change.
- **`priority` stays out of scope** — the ask names status only.

## Existing state

- The selection-list metadata panel renders `Blocked By  WL-xxx — <title>` rows via `buildMetadataPanelLines()` (paired with `pairMetaRows()`) in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`, one row per active blocker at the end of the metadata section (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8). The flicker fix (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP) makes the resolved rows survive refreshes via a signature-keyed cache in `runWorklistTui`; while a re-resolve is in flight the last known value is rendered (single-flight).
- `BlockerRef` (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`) is `{ id; title }`; `fetchBlockersForItem()` resolves edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`, enriches each non-terminal edge's `stage` via `fetchItemDetails` (for the `isActiveBlocker` predicate) and pushes `{ id, title }` — the edge's `status` is currently dropped.
- `wl dep list <id> --json` returns outbound edges with `id`, `title`, `status`, `priority`, `direction: depends-on`.
- The Herdr detail view (`formatDetailContent()` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) renders the metadata table but deliberately does NOT render `Blocked By` rows — the divergence is documented at the `formatDetailContent` docstring (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP AC-5). Detail-view scrolling is handled by `detailScrollOffset` with a clamp based on the full content height.
- The TUI details pane precedent ("Blocking"/"Blocked by" links, WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU / WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1) lives in the pi TUI extension, outside this change.

## Desired change

1. **Data:** extend `BlockerRef` with the edge's `status`; thread it through `fetchBlockersForItem`.
2. **Preview:** append the status (icon + text via `statusIcon`, honouring `noIcons`) to each `Blocked By` value in `buildMetadataPanelLines()` — e.g.
   ```
   Blocked By  WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W — worklist.ts: pre-dialog gate 🟠 in_progress
   ```
3. **Detail view:** resolve the active blockers for the detail item (same single-flight/cache pattern as the preview loop) and render one `Blocked By` row per blocker after the metadata table (before the description body), updating the detail scroll-height clamp so the rows are reachable; fail-open.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `BlockerRef` gains `status`; `fetchBlockersForItem` passes the edge status through (no extra lookups).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildMetadataPanelLines()` (preview rows) appends status icon+text; `formatDetailContent()`/`formatDetail()` render `Blocked By` rows after the metadata table; `runWorklistTui` detail path resolves blockers single-flight; detail scroll clamp accounts for the new rows.
- `packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts` — reuse `isActiveBlocker()` (no change expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — reuse `parseDepListBlockersOutput()` (no change expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` / `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — reuse `statusIcon()` (no change expected).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — preview + detail `Blocked By` status rendering tests, omission, fail-open.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher-blockers.test.ts` — blocker status passthrough tests.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-blocked-by-cache.test.ts` — detail-view lookup does not reintroduce flicker; preview unchanged.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `Blocked By` status rendering (preview + detail view).

## Related work

- **Show what an item is blocked on (WL-0MV8EZRDJ001TDA8)** — completed; added the preview's `Blocked By` rows. This item extends them with status and ports the rows to the detail view.
- **Herdr selection list: 'Blocked By' metadata line flickers endlessly (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP)** — completed; the flicker fix whose AC-5 documented the detail-view divergence this item reverses.
- **Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9)** — completed; icon+text meta-row conventions used here.
- **Herdr selection list should show dependency-blocked items (WL-0MV6TFX0600145M2)** — completed; `--include-blocked` so blocked items appear. Related because blocked-item visibility.
- **Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI (WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU)** / **TUI: Render dependency links in Details pane (WL-0MP15T47A001OCB1)** — completed; pi TUI details-pane "Blocking"/"Blocked by" precedent (out of scope here).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** reversing the detail-view divergence could expand into a general dependency browser (inbound "Blocking" rows, click-to-open, `+N more`). Explicitly out of scope; any such opportunity should be recorded as a linked follow-up work item, not absorbed here.
- **Performance risk:** detail-view blocker lookup must follow the preview's single-flight + signature-keyed cache so rapid view switches do not spawn duplicate `wl dep list` processes or flicker. Mitigation: reuse the established cache/fail-open pattern (WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP).
- **Scroll-regression risk:** new detail rows must be included in the detail scroll-height clamp, or they become unreachable when the view scrolls. Mitigation: update the height calc alongside the render.
- **Flicker-regression risk (detail view):** if the detail blocker lookup were wired without the signature-keyed cache/single-flight pattern, rapid view switches could re-introduce the WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP flicker class. Mitigation: reuse the established cache + fail-open pattern; add a regression test that repeated detail lookups render the resolved rows stably.
- **Assumption (Q1-A):** status is shown on both the selection-list preview AND the detail view (operator choice b).
- **Assumption (Q2-A):** status renders as icon + text suffix, consistent with the Status row convention (operator choice b).
- **Assumption:** the blocker's `status` value comes straight from the `wl dep list` edge (`status` field); it is already present, so no extra lookups. A blocker edge without a status still renders ID + title alone.
- **Decision (operator, Q2 note):** `priority` stays out of scope — the ask names status only and the operator did not opt to include it.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Scope: the item mentions 'selection list preview and detail view', but the Herdr detail view currently shows no `Blocked By` rows at all (documented divergence WL-0MV8Q5X8U004KKAP AC-5). (a) Add blocker status only to the selection-list metadata panel rows; (b) add status to the metadata panel AND add `Blocked By` rows (with status) to the detail view, reversing the divergence." — Answer (operator): **(b)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: the reporter's wording names both surfaces; status should be visible wherever blocker information is shown, and the detail view gap is acknowledged.
- Q2: "How should the blocker's status render in a `Blocked By` row? (a) plain status in parentheses, no icon; (b) icon + plain text suffix, consistent with the Status row convention; (c) status appended with a separator, no icon." — Answer (operator): **(b)**. Source: interactive reply. Rationale: consistent with the icon+text convention used by every other meta row (WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9), so the blocker's state is scannable at a glance.
